kind: Single-agent review of observer decoding performance change
invariants: The same single memory(p,n*8) read occurs on each call; no cached runtime memory or new reads, mappings, tokens, permissions, deadlines or guest writes.
For every complete n-word read, unsigned little-endian Q decoding returns the same Python integer list in original order, including high-bit words and zero count.

Every existing ownership/table/register/content/retirement assertion remains present and receives all words. A truncated read fails closed instead of returning partial words; GDB read_memory normally returns the requested length or raises.

Only the frame_memory embedded observer changes. The frame_root predecessor decoder is retained as an independent comparison in four tests. No compiler, native kernel, authority or core-language semantics change in this performance fix.

Profile timing is diagnostic only, not full native acceptance or a proof of full memory safety. Separate VM entropy makes two prefix states differ in captured data/hash fields; no whole-state equality claim.
